etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Latin verbōsus (“prolix, wordy, verbose”). Verbōsus is derived from verbum (“word”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *werh₁- (“to say, speak”)) + -ōsus (suffix meaning ‘full of, overly, prone to’ forming adjectives from nouns). Equivalent to verb (“word”) +‎ -ose (“-ful”), literally “full of words”.
senses: Containing or using more words than necessary; long-winded, wordy. [from 17th c.]
(computing) Producing detailed output for diagnostic purposes.
